answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: Yes, skip the 16-miler. A long run on Wed of race week does not add fitness, it only costs you freshness that you cannot buy back by Sunday. The last 20-miler on Oct 4 is the one that counts, and it is already in the bank. If you need to feel ready, the Wed session with 3 miles at goal pace will do that job without digging a hole.

new.analysis:
## Why this plan

Everything from here is about arriving fresh, not fitter. You cannot add fitness in six days, but you can lose freshness by cramming, so the week drops volume to about half of last week and keeps just enough faster running to stay sharp.

The one bit of quality on Wed is short on purpose: a few miles at goal pace to remind the legs what 8:35/mi feels like, nothing that leaves a mark. Fri is a full rest day, and Sat is a tiny shakeout with a couple of strides so you wake up on race morning feeling springy, not stale.

## How you ran last week

You followed the planned week almost to the mile: easy 6 on Tue, the 8 with marathon-pace work on Wed, easy 5 on Thu, 3-mile shakeout on Sat, long 12 on Sun. Nothing skipped, nothing overrun, no pain, sleep solid. That is exactly what a first taper week should look like.

The heavy, flat legs you flagged are a normal taper signal, not lost fitness. Heart rate on easy runs is still 139 at 9:51/mi, the same as three weeks ago, and the 20-miler back on Oct 4 held 9:59/mi with only 5 bpm of drift. The fitness is there.

## Race-day shape

Target pace for sub-3:45 is about 8:35/mi. Your Wednesday marathon-pace work has been sitting right there at 8:32 to 8:40, which is a good sign. The trap on race day is going out at 8:20 because you feel fresh; hold 8:35 through 10K, settle in, and the race is yours in the back half.

I will send a short race-day note mid-week with fuelling and pacing cues. Eat normally, sleep when you can, and keep the shoes you have been running in.
